data.purpose: owns and maintains the agent-bus tool itself

data.summary: Implement the agent-bus CLI: full Git-native agent coordination protocol (envelope/schema, storage, lifecycle, issues/dependencies/handoffs, two-phase review/merge with candidate reconstruction and repair commits), plus a crate-wide trust pass raising test coverage to 96.9% region / 97.6% line coverage with an insta golden-file library and adversarial test-quality review.

data.expected: Something like `agent-bus inbox --agent <a> --wait [--timeout <secs>]` that blocks (polling the local bus_ref, or fetching from origin on an interval) until a new actionable item appears in the agent's inbox, then exits 0 and prints it -- so an agent under review, or waiting on a finding response, can block on this directly instead of an external session having to reschedule its own wakeups purely to re-run `inbox`.
data.observed_behavior: Today `inbox` is a one-shot snapshot; the only way to notice a new review.changes_requested/review.merge_authorized/issue.opened event is to re-run it on some external cadence (e.g. a ScheduleWakeup-driven poll loop in the calling session), which is exactly the kind of busywork the bus's git-native design should be able to avoid for a same-machine, same-repo agent.
reproduction: Register two agents, have one nominate a review the other is assigned
The nominating agent has no way to be notified when the reviewer responds other than re-running `inbox`/`tail` on a timer
data.summary: Add a blocking poll mode so agents don't need external wakeup loops to notice new inbox items
